validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node 24 (v24.14.0) and no installed dependencies. The script loads the submitted harness modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs, so runtime/drive/tools.ts (real recoverToolInvocation), execution/tools.ts (real executeToolCall) and execution/effect-gate.ts (real createGate) all execute live; only checkpoint storage, progress transport, hook delivery and tool bodies are promise-based fakes. Assertions use uncaught node:assert/strict checks and promise ordering (microtask settle loop, no timers, randomness, network or credentials). Repaired tree: exit 0, 'execution lifecycle fences: all cross-module assertions passed'. Cross-module coverage: (1) gate close-then-beginAbort still refuses admit with the terminal error and keeps signal.reason terminal, close wins over a pending abort, and the first cancellation wins between repeated aborts; (2) a closed gate plus late beginAbort makes executeToolCall refuse with the terminal error without invoking the tool or delivering updates; (3) updates fired after tool completion are sealed (both plain and {checkpoint:true}) while mid-flight live and checkpoint updates are still delivered; (4) cancelled safe/safe recovery records only read+publish (no clear, no invoke, no update, no tool context) and stages the interruption marker with checkpoint content/details; (5) non-cancelled safe/safe recovery completes the full clear -> invoke -> effect-complete -> seal -> drain -> publish sequence exactly once and preserves details {kept:true} and usage {output:3}, and a non-safe replay still stages the checkpoint outcome. Regression detection was verified locally by restoring each source file alone to its faulty baseline (beginAbort === 'aborting' guard, acceptingUpdates = true in finally, missing !cancelled guard): each run exited 1 with an AssertionError (late beginAbort reopened the closed gate / updates emitted after completion must be sealed / a cancelled recovery must not clear its checkpoint), never an import error, crash or timeout; the sources were then restored and the suite re-passed.

claims.evidence: recoverToolInvocation ignored its cancelled argument; now the safe-replay branch requires !cancelled, so a cancelled recovery reads the checkpoint and publishes a single interrupted outcome without clearReplayCheckpoint or performToolInvocation.

claims.claim: A completed tool can emit new updates
claims.evidence: executeToolCall reset its update latch to true in the completion finally; it now seals (acceptingUpdates = false) so live and checkpoint-bearing callbacks after completion are dropped.

claims.claim: beginAbort cannot reopen a closed gate or replace its terminal error
claims.evidence: beginAbort only short-circuited while aborting and overwrote the closed state; it now returns unless the gate is open, keeping the terminal error and abort reason authoritative.

claims.claim: Non-cancelled safe/safe recovery must still complete, preserve usage/details and publish once
claims.evidence: The regression asserts the full clear -> invoke -> effect-complete -> seal -> drain -> publish sequence with one publish, details {kept:true} and usage {output:3}, and that mid-flight updates are still delivered.
